title: The Lesson I Learned When Lot Chose What Looked Good
paragraphs:
The Lesson I Learned When Lot Chose What Looked Good
(Genesis 13:10)

Lot looked up.
And what he saw was beautiful.

Green plains.
Water everywhere.
A land that looked like blessing.
But not everything that glitters is God’s will.

Genesis 13:10 shows Lot lifting his eyes toward the well-watered plain of Jordan. It looked like Eden. It looked like favor. It looked like the obvious choice. But what looked good to his eyes led him closer to Sodom.
And that’s the lesson that cut deep into me:

What looks fruitful can still be fatal.
What feels right can still pull you away from God.

Lot chose by sight.
Abram stayed by faith.

One moved toward comfort.
The other stayed where trust was required.

And here’s what we miss:
The danger was not just the land Lot chose.
It was the heart behind the choice.

He saw prosperity.
But he did not stop to ask about purity.
He saw opportunity.
But he ignored the atmosphere.
He saw what could grow his wealth, but not what could poison his soul.
How many of us have done the same?

Chosen relationships because they looked exciting.
Taken opportunities because they looked successful.
Walked into places that fed the flesh while starving the spirit.

Beloved, the eye is a poor master.
Sight can seduce.
Feelings can lie.
Culture can decorate destruction until it looks harmless.

But God does not lead His children by glitter.
He leads them by truth.

Lot’s story warns us:
The best-looking option is not always the God-breathed option.
And yet this is where grace walks in.

Because all of us, in some way, have chosen Sodom-looking fields.
We have all drifted toward what pleased us more than what pleased God.
But Jesus came for people who chose badly.
He came for the wandering, the compromised, the near-Sodom soul.

At the cross, Christ took the punishment for our foolish choices.
In His resurrection, He opened the way back for us—not just to regret, but to repentance.
Not just to shame, but to restoration.

So here is the lesson:
Don’t choose by what looks good. Choose by what leads you closer to God.
Because a peaceful-looking field without God is still a dangerous place.
But even a hard place with God is safer than abundance without Him.

Lift your eyes, yes.
But bow your heart first.

“Walk by faith, not by sight.”
That is still the safer road.
